sector: A contemporary seasonal tasting counter, twenty two seats around the pass, one menu a night, four nights a week.
founded_place_size: A twenty two seat tasting counter on the coast of New England, one seasonal menu at 135 dollars a head served four nights a week.
about: OSTRA is a counter, not a dining room: guests sit around the pass for one seasonal tasting menu at 135 dollars a head. The room is near black, spare and unhurried, and the photography is meant to feel like walking into it rather than like an advertisement. One plate at a time, on a dark ground, with light that still reads as light.
audience: Guests aged 30 to 55 booking an occasion around six weeks ahead, who expect calm and consideration rather than volume.
price_positioning: A 135 dollar seasonal tasting counter. The grammar is a near black ground, one plate per frame, generous emptiness, restrained saturation, and speculars on sauce and glass that read as light rather than as blown white or flat grey. Never a bright, crowded bistro look, and never near monochrome art photography in which the food cannot be read.

palette.name: Near Black
palette.role: mandatory on the menu announcement and the reservation story
palette.usage: The page ground of the menu announcement and the reservation story, and the ground Bone type sits on. On the dish tiles it is used only for a band or panel behind the caption, if there is one.

palette.name: Slate Pass
palette.usage: An alternative to Near Black for a band or panel behind type, matching the slate pass in the photographs. Never a type colour.

palette.name: Ash Grey
palette.usage: Thin dividers or outlines; on a Bone ground only, small fine print, as the date line on ostra_menu_card_autumn.pdf. Never a ground, and never type on Near Black, Slate Pass or a photograph.

palette.name: Bone
palette.usage: The wordmark, the house mark reproduced from ostra_house_mark_plate.jpg as a flat mark, every course title and caption, every detail line, any fine print and the booking or reservation action. On the menu announcement and the reservation story it sits only on Near Black or Slate Pass; on the dish tiles the caption may also sit on the dark slate of the photograph.

palette.name: Subdued Brass
palette.usage: The 0.4 pt hairline under the O S T R A wordmark, cut to exactly the wordmark width, and at most a small label, as the pairing-flight label on ostra_menu_card_autumn.pdf. Never a ground, panel, button, wordmark, house mark or course title.

typography: OSTRA sets four steps. Step 01, display and H1, is Recife Display Light at 52 px on 56 px leading, tracked minus 10 thousandths, for the announcing course title, as in Oyster, cucumber, elderflower; the wordmark sets in the same face, O S T R A in caps tracked 320 thousandths, centred over a 0.4 pt Subdued Brass hairline cut to exactly the wordmark width. Step 02, the subheading, is Recife Display Light at 40 px on 44 px, tracked minus 5 thousandths, for the dish tile course title, as in Hake, brown butter, sea kale, and it sets at 15 pt on 21 pt on the printed guest card. Step 03, body, is Suisse Int'l Light at 22 px on 32 px leading, tracked 60 thousandths, Bone on Near Black, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line, as in: Five courses. One seating. Please arrive as the light goes; that 60 thousandths is the brand's own figure and is kept rather than closed to zero. Step 04, fine print, is Suisse Int'l Light at 16 px on 24 px, tracked 80 thousandths, as in Twenty two seats. Four nights a week. Bookings six weeks ahead; that size is the one figure the existing notes never stated, set proportionate under the 22 px detail line.
voice: Spare and understated, the voice of a room that lets the plate speak. Example line the brand would write: "Five courses. One seating. Please arrive as the light goes."
brand_assets_status: There are no editable brand files. The per guest menu card survives only as the old printer's press PDF, and the printer has been lost, so the room hand writes about forty cards a night. A dark mode site reference screengrab was supplied as mood only, and course titles come spelled as the kitchen spells them.
values: Honesty of the room and one plate at a time: the photographs are this kitchen's real plates, and restraint is what the guest is paying for.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is always O S T R A in Recife Display Light caps tracked 320 thousandths, open enough that the five letters nearly come apart, centred over a 0.4 pt Subdued Brass hairline cut to exactly the wordmark width. That extreme air between letters registers first.
rules: Never set a course title in the sans.
The wordmark is always O S T R A in Recife Display Light caps tracked 320 thousandths, centred over a 0.4 pt Subdued Brass hairline cut to exactly the wordmark width.
The hairline is cut to the wordmark width exactly, never run wide.
Course titles come spelled as the kitchen spells them and are never corrected.
Detail lines stay Suisse Int'l Light, Bone on Near Black, tracked 60 thousandths.
One plate per frame on a near black ground: type keeps its distance and never crowds the picture.
Generous emptiness and restrained saturation, never a bright crowded bistro look.

palette_rules.distribution: The page ground of the menu announcement and the reservation story is Near Black, and Slate Pass may be a band or panel behind type. On the menu announcement and the reservation story, type sits only on Near Black or Slate Pass; on the dish tiles, the caption may sit on the photograph's own dark slate or on a Near Black or Slate Pass band. The wordmark, the house mark, course titles, captions, detail lines, fine print and the booking or reservation action are Bone, and no type sits over the plate or the food. Ash Grey is never type on these dark pieces, only thin dividers or outlines, and Subdued Brass is only the wordmark hairline or a small label; together they cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or to type, type carries no outline stroke, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: a band behind type is a solid block. Every export is fully opaque, because the delivery platforms put every picture on a white card.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; the old press card's Warm-Ink #3A2A22 is not a palette colour. Subdued Brass is a flat colour, never a metallic, foil or gradient effect. No bright or saturated accent colour: never the bright, crowded bistro look.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette, toned to near monochrome or pushed to bright saturation. The slate in the photographs keeps its own tone and texture and is not crushed or recoloured to the Near Black hex. The thirteen frames read as one room under one white balance. The one white balance is neutral: pale plates read neutral, neither green, cool nor candle-warm. Speculars on sauce and glass read as light, not as flat grey.
